title: Memes in the Wild: Assessing the Generalizability of the Hateful Memes Challenge Dataset
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures general hate speech in memes, comparing a synthetic dataset (Facebook's Hateful Memes Challenge) with 'in the wild' memes from Pinterest. It does not specifically measure or analyze hate speech related to faith or religion, focusing instead on technical generalizability challenges like OCR performance and image/text modality differences.
findings: The paper presents no findings related to religion. The only mention of a related topic is the identification of bigrams like 'isis strip' and 'ilhan omar' as common in the non-hateful Facebook meme dataset, which is an observation about dataset content rather than a finding on religious hate or bias.
